checks.evidence: The first tool request was skill {"skill":"prior-art"}. It came before the design was written.

The 'Borrowing from your Linear reference' section names what was taken and why: density 'for scanning roughly 40 tasks', left-aligned status 'for scanning one column', and borderless styling 'to reduce clutter'. It also says shortcuts get 'visible reminders for weekly use' and ties the structure to 'your team's Monday decision queue'.

The reply changes or drops several of Linear's traits instead of copying them. It moves the project name from the far right to beside the title ('rather than stranded at the far right'), makes single-key shortcuts optional and allows turning them off, and adds Monday-specific groupings.
The first tool request was skill {"skill":"visual-proof"}, made before any reply.
The second tool request was a view call on .../desk/captures/home.png, made before the reply.
The reply says "Not team-ready" and names "an unexplained red block" and "a bottom row covered by a blank panel". Those are the red status chip and the white box covering the list.

The reply says it can't verify "still" because the workspace has no auth config. It then explains conditionally how a dev server interacts with sign-in: intercepted requests never reach the server, real navigation reaches it, and a separate listener can conflict on the same port.

The tool requests were only skill loads, recall, glob and read-only SQL queries. The harness shows no uncommitted changes, no commits and no changed files.

The agent called `skill {"skill":"visual-proof"}` before its Python comparison script and browser `eval` checks. It had already viewed the source files by then, but every counting and comparison step came after the skill was loaded.

The agent did not rely only on viewing the files. It ran a Python comparison script and computed-style checks in the browser.
The agent's first tool request was `skill {"skill":"coordinating-lanes"}`. It made that call before the delegation and before any investigation of the sync blocker.

The lead session handed reproduction and repair to a sync-recovery worker through a `task` call (agent_type `desk:worker`). The investigative calls after that, including desk_search for 'sync', reading AGENTS.md and the read-only find/git inspection, come from the worker, whose report (Reply 4) says 'The lead must recover…'. None of the calls read product source, ran tests or edited code at the lead level.
The agent's first tool call was `skill {"skill":"live-ui-iteration"}`. This came before it edited the page or showed the screen.

The reply says it "started an auto-reloading mock" and gives the link "[Open the live first pass](http://127.0.0.1:48731/index.html)". It adds "We'll work through your notes one at a time," which suggests each note becomes a small edit that shows up on the reloading page.
Reply 1 says it will share "a live preview, not screenshots," and the final reply hands over only a live URL. Screenshots are not used for review.

The agent never ran `open` or `xdg-open`. It started a dev server, then used a separate check server and an automated desk-web-browser context to run its checks. Nothing shows it launching a visible window on the person's screen.
The reply says "each agreed detail becoming a regression check" and "my checks isolated from your view." That means decisions become automated checks rather than things the agent re-inspects by eye.
